text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.69% today to close at $424.89, continuing a sharp nine-day rally that's added nearly 10% to the stock price. The climb reflects a combination of tight refining conditions and elevated crude prices: US oil is trading at $107 a barrel while refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, and diesel inventories have fallen to just 107.9 million barrels. These conditions support higher margins for refiners, which buy crude and sell refined products like gasoline and diesel at the pump and to commercial buyers.

The broader Middle East conflict—including Saudi pipeline disruptions and the Houthi-Saudi exchange of attacks this week—has kept oil prices elevated despite Saudi Arabia's efforts to reassure markets by offering additional crude exports. Diesel prices reaching record highs are particularly meaningful for Marathon because diesel commands premium prices relative to gasoline in high-cost environments, bolstering refiner profitability even as the company's stock has already run up significantly in recent days.
